item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-1fbc524a4429d2b1","start_unit":6,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"The government adopted interministerial measures establishing mediation committees for children’s courts and peace courts in most provinces; 83 committees with 249 members were installed, but only 80 members from eight provinces received training and financial support, while national and provincial permanent secretariats were created.","question_ids":["3B.4","6B.9","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The document reports implementation mainly from 2018 onward, not specifically 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes these measures to the DRC government and provincial authorities during Félix Tshisekedi’s administration.","limitations":["Implementation and outcomes are incompletely documented.","The supplied extraction is corrupted UTF-16 HTML and does not provide a direct 2023 status."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1fbc524a4429d2b1","start_unit":8,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"The DRC created the national Agency for the Prevention and Fight against Trafficking in Persons by a 2019 ordinance, assigning it duties to develop strategy, disseminate regulations, report trafficking to security and judicial institutions, combat impunity, support investigations, assist victims, compensate victims, and publish annual reporting; a strategic plan was implemented from 2021 and 393 trafficking cases were recorded in 2021, including 314 female victims.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.10","6B.3","6B.9","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The institutional measures and statistics precede 2023; the report does not establish 2023 results.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes creation and operation of the agency to the DRC government.","limitations":["The reported case count is for 2021.","No evidence is supplied on prosecutions, compensation, or outcome effectiveness by 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1fbc524a4429d2b1","start_unit":24,"end_unit":25,"fact_summary":"The government reported that child trafficking, child prostitution, and child pornography were punishable by five to twenty years’ imprisonment, including when committed abroad; it also stated that a draft anti-trafficking law was before Parliament and that public-sector salaries had been increased by 30 percent in the second quarter and 45 percent in the third quarter of 2022.","question_ids":["3B.7","6B.3","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The legal and wage measures are reported for 2022 or earlier, not 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the criminal-law framework and wage measures to the government and Parliament.","limitations":["The extraction does not establish enforcement or actual incidence reduction.","The wage increases are not linked to a specific ruler directive in the supplied text."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1fbc524a4429d2b1","start_unit":26,"end_unit":27,"fact_summary":"The national child-protection policy promised in 2017 had still not been elaborated; a draft decree establishing the National Children’s Council had been adopted by government and sent to the Prime Minister for signature, with adoption conditioned on signing that decree.","question_ids":["6B.1","6B.9","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"This finding concerns the status reported before the document’s 2023 receipt and does not demonstrate completion in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the pending policy and draft decree to the DRC government.","limitations":["The text does not state whether the decree was ultimately signed.","No budget or measurable outcome is supplied."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1fbc524a4429d2b1","start_unit":27,"end_unit":29,"fact_summary":"The 2022 budget included 2.7 billion Congolese francs for the child-protection directorate and ministry, intended to finance child-protection committees, mediation committees nationwide, and a campaign against child marriage; the government also described a transition toward program budgeting with defined objectives and expected results.","question_ids":["6B.1","6B.3","6B.6","6B.9","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The budget evidence is for 2022 and earlier, not the 2023 period itself.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the budget allocation and program-budget reform to the DRC government.","limitations":["The extraction does not show actual disbursement or execution of the allocation.","The report does not establish whether the funded activities achieved their intended results."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1fbc524a4429d2b1","start_unit":33,"end_unit":35,"fact_summary":"The government had not established a centralized child-specific data-collection system; instead, sectors maintained separate systems, while a draft decree for the National Children’s Council proposed a national database on children’s conditions.","question_ids":["6B.5","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The finding describes the situation before or around 2023 and is not a 2023 outcome measurement.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the missing centralized system and proposed database to the DRC government.","limitations":["Existing sectoral systems may still provide usable data.","The extraction does not state whether the proposed database was implemented by 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1fbc524a4429d2b1","start_unit":36,"end_unit":38,"fact_summary":"The National Human Rights Commission had obtained A status under the Paris Principles; its permanent subcommission on women’s and children’s rights received complaints from parents and guardians, and provincial CNDH coordinations monitored children’s rights, including children deprived of liberty.","question_ids":["3B.4","4B.4","6B.5","8B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The institutional finding predates or overlaps the target period but is not dated specifically to 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report describes the institutions as state human-rights mechanisms operating under the DRC framework; it does not attribute their independence directly to Tshisekedi personally.","limitations":["The supplied text does not quantify complaint resolution or remedies.","Institutional existence does not establish effective independence in practice."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1fbc524a4429d2b1","start_unit":39,"end_unit":40,"fact_summary":"Under the 2001 law on nonprofit associations, provisional authorization allowed registered provincial associations to operate for six months pending legal personality, but the report states that the automatic grant of legal personality did not function in practice and that several civil-society organizations remained outside state annex budgets.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.6","6B.7","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The legal framework and implementation finding are not confined to 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the authorization process to the Justice Ministry and provincial governors, without identifying a personal presidential decision.","limitations":["The extraction does not provide the number of affected organizations or later corrective action.","The budget exclusion finding is descriptive rather than causal."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1fbc524a4429d2b1","start_unit":41,"end_unit":46,"fact_summary":"The Mining Code required environmental impact studies, environmental-management plans, financial guarantees for rehabilitation, restrictions on land occupation, and liability for contamination and other harms; however, a 2020 ministerial visit found extractive industries in Lualaba and Haut-Katanga were not respecting operating standards and had very negative effects through water pollution and soil degradation. The DRC joined voluntary security and human-rights principles for extractive companies in 2022.","question_ids":["3B.7","5B.4","5B.5","5B.7","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The adverse institutional finding is from 2020 and the voluntary-principles accession from 2022, not 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the legal safeguards and 2022 accession to the DRC state; it does not establish Félix Tshisekedi’s personal role.","limitations":["The text does not report enforcement actions against noncompliant firms.","Voluntary principles do not demonstrate binding compliance."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1fbc524a4429d2b1","start_unit":47,"end_unit":48,"fact_summary":"Parliament adopted an organic law protecting persons with disabilities in September 2021, but by the reporting period it awaited promulgation; the report also states that no global strategy or study existed to eliminate discrimination against vulnerable groups.","question_ids":["4B.7","6B.3","6B.8","8B.2","8B.6","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The law and gap are reported before 2023 and do not establish promulgation or implementation during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes adoption to Parliament and the pending promulgation to the Head of State’s office.","limitations":["The extraction does not confirm whether promulgation later occurred.","No implementation budget or enforcement data is supplied."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1fbc524a4429d2b1","start_unit":51,"end_unit":52,"fact_summary":"The government program identified eradication of armed groups in eastern DRC as a first peacebuilding pillar, alongside reintegration of demobilized youth, creation of trained and equipped elite brigades, and continuation of a state of siege in North Kivu and Ituri since May 2021; a joint technical group monitored children and armed conflicts.","question_ids":["2B.4","2B.5","2B.7","2B.10","3B.2","3B.6","3B.9","8B.1","8B.2","8B.5","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The program and state-of-siege facts cover periods before and up to 2023, but the extraction does not provide a 2023 evaluation of results.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the peacebuilding program and state of siege to the DRC government under the Head of State.","limitations":["The text gives objectives and monitoring arrangements but not independent outcome evidence.","It does not assess civilian-protection consequences of the state of siege."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1fbc524a4429d2b1","start_unit":53,"end_unit":55,"fact_summary":"The health development plan set three strategic axes—service improvement and continuity, support to health-system pillars, and governance—and reported implementation including rehabilitation of 73 health centers, construction of 32 centers, equipment for 28 health zones, and measurable gains in family-planning, fistula treatment, malaria prevention, assisted childbirth, and curative-service use.","question_ids":["6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.4","6B.6","6B.9","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The reported implementation and outcome figures largely concern 2013–2018 or earlier, not 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes implementation to the DRC government with international partner support.","limitations":["The causal contribution of the president is not isolated from donors or subnational actors.","Reported gains are not contemporaneous with 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1fbc524a4429d2b1","start_unit":60,"end_unit":63,"fact_summary":"Birth registration increased from 25 percent in 2014 to 40 percent in 2018, supported by a national strategy, expanded civil-registry offices, trained personnel, and donor support; substantial disparities remained between urban and rural areas and across wealth and maternal-education groups, with some provinces recording rates as low as 5–17 percent.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.3","6B.8","6B.10","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The quantitative findings are for 2014–2018 and do not measure 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the strategy and administrative expansion to the DRC government with World Bank and UNICEF support.","limitations":["The figures are not contemporaneous with the target period.","The extraction does not establish whether disparities narrowed by 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1fbc524a4429d2b1","start_unit":66,"end_unit":67,"fact_summary":"The justice-reform plan proposed pilot state education and rehabilitation establishments for children deprived of liberty in 2022; meanwhile, COVID-19 prompted authorities to empty special juvenile quarters and place children in private social institutions.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.5","3B.7","3B.9","6B.6","8B.2","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The measures concern 2020–2022 and do not establish 2023 implementation.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the decisions to justice authorities and the government.","limitations":["The extraction does not state how many children were transferred or the conditions in receiving institutions.","No evaluation of the pilot establishments is provided."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1fbc524a4429d2b1","start_unit":69,"end_unit":72,"fact_summary":"The revised national strategy against gender-based violence included prevention, women’s empowerment, education, population protection, holistic victim care, justice and anti-impunity, and data collection; President Félix Tshisekedi launched a zero-tolerance campaign in June 2021 extending to 2023, including planned equitable trials, reparations funds, transitional justice, school training, victim-protection laws, and gender-equality measures.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.4","3B.7","3B.9","6B.3","6B.8","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The campaign began in 2021 and was planned through 2023; the supplied text does not verify completion or results by the end of 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report directly attributes the campaign launch to President Félix Tshisekedi.","limitations":["Most listed items are objectives or planned measures rather than verified outcomes.","No independent assessment of implementation or impunity reduction is supplied."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1fbc524a4429d2b1","start_unit":73,"end_unit":74,"fact_summary":"Seven provinces adopted the 2017 national action plan against child marriage; three provinces conducted sensitization activities, and the report states that reported child-maltreatment cases linked to witchcraft accusations became rarer, possibly following sensitization through community and religious leaders. A free 116 hotline was established for children in distress.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.7","6B.3","6B.8","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The reported provincial implementation and trend are from periods before 2023 and are not a 2023 outcome evaluation.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the action plan and hotline to the DRC government and provincial authorities, with NGO support.","limitations":["The report qualifies the decline as possible and does not provide a quantified time series.","The extraction does not show hotline usage or remedy outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1fbc524a4429d2b1","start_unit":77,"end_unit":81,"fact_summary":"A provincial zero-street-children center in Haut-Katanga was created to accommodate 500 children and had received 140 children in 2020, with 80 receiving vocational training; revised adoption rules strengthened public review, but international adoption was suspended pending a decree establishing a central adoption authority, affecting new cases while 1,200 previously suspended dossiers had been cleared between April and December 2016.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.3","6B.7","6B.9","8B.2","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The center data are from 2020 and the adoption data are historical; they do not establish 2023 outcomes.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the center to the provincial government and adoption reforms to the national government and Justice Ministry.","limitations":["The extraction does not show the center’s later operation or capacity.","The adoption figures concern 2016 and cannot be treated as 2023 performance."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1fbc524a4429d2b1","start_unit":82,"end_unit":85,"fact_summary":"The 2019–2023 government program planned a disability-assistance policy and created a delegated ministry for persons with disabilities; an organic disability-rights law was adopted by Parliament in 2021 but awaited promulgation. The report notes that about 45 percent of children with motor disabilities and 75 percent with mental disabilities aged 6–11 were out of school, compared with 28.7 percent of non-disabled peers.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.3","6B.8","6B.9","8B.1","8B.2","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The program period reaches 2023, but the outcome figures are historical and the text does not confirm 2023 implementation.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the program and delegated ministry to the DRC government and the law to Parliament.","limitations":["The law’s promulgation status is unresolved.","The education disparity figures are not dated to 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1fbc524a4429d2b1","start_unit":86,"end_unit":88,"fact_summary":"The education strategy proposed specialized schools and inclusive education for children with disabilities; 115 specialized education centers were affiliated with ACHAC, and a pilot project worked with 12 schools in four Kinshasa communes. The government also reported that primary education had been free since 2019, with enrollment rising from two million pupils in the first year to four million in 2022.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.3","6B.8","6B.9","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The enrollment result reaches 2022; the document does not provide a 2023 update.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes free primary education and related implementation to the DRC government, with donor and civil-society support.","limitations":["Enrollment growth does not establish attendance, quality, or equitable access.","The role of Félix Tshisekedi is not separately quantified from government and partners."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1fbc524a4429d2b1","start_unit":97,"end_unit":100,"fact_summary":"The health program reported implementation of infrastructure, equipment, financing, and human-resource measures; from the 100-day program, 46.16 million US dollars, or 9.45 percent of the total, was allocated to health to finalize 31 centers, complete 51, equip 32, construct a hospital in Ituri, and purchase vaccines and essential medicines.","question_ids":["6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.4","6B.6","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The 100-day program began in 2019; these figures are not 2023 results.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the allocation to the government’s 100-day program under the Head of State.","limitations":["The supplied text does not establish completion or service-quality outcomes for the listed projects.","External financing and implementation partners are material contributors."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1fbc524a4429d2b1","start_unit":103,"end_unit":108,"fact_summary":"The HIV program reported expanded prevention, testing, treatment, laboratory, and monitoring systems, including a 50 percent reduction among people living with HIV and increased antiretroviral coverage from 16 percent in 2012 to 42.5 percent in 2016; pediatric treatment coverage rose from 9 percent to 29 percent, and new infections among infants of seropositive mothers fell by 62 percent.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.6","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The statistics are primarily for 2012–2017 and do not measure 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the program to the DRC government with international partner support.","limitations":["The date and definition of the reported 50 percent reduction are unclear in the extraction.","No 2023 update or attribution of causal responsibility to Tshisekedi is provided."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1fbc524a4429d2b1","start_unit":116,"end_unit":121,"fact_summary":"The 2019–2023 government program made poverty reduction and social marginalization a pillar and proposed potable-water access, renewable energy, electricity expansion, coordinated investment, provincial water works, microcredit, vocational training, and social centers; the 100-day program included planned water-treatment plants in Kinshasa and Lemba and water projects in multiple provinces, while primary education was reported free nationwide from 2019 and reached four million children by 2022.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The program spans 2019–2023, but the supplied text mainly reports plans and outcomes through 2022.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the program and 100-day initiatives to the DRC government and Head of State.","limitations":["Several measures are proposed rather than demonstrated as completed.","The document does not provide 2023 execution or distributional results."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1fbc524a4429d2b1","start_unit":123,"end_unit":130,"fact_summary":"The education program was supported by an 800 million US dollar World Bank project; reported measures included direct budget support, teacher salaries, school operating costs, resource-management systems, and the integration of 144,944 new teachers into payroll listings, with 58,000 new-unit teachers paid during the final quarter of 2020. Teacher salaries rose from 90 to 207 US dollars in 2019, but transport and housing allowances were paid to only 62,859 of 445,024 teachers.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.7","6B.2","6B.4","6B.5","6B.10","8B.3","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The quantitative figures concern 2019–2020 and do not establish 2023 performance.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes payroll and salary measures to the DRC government, with World Bank support.","limitations":["The extraction does not show later payment coverage or whether payroll reforms reduced fraud.","Donor financing materially supported the program."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1fbc524a4429d2b1","start_unit":131,"end_unit":135,"fact_summary":"In August 2019 the DRC hosted 538,706 refugees and 10,144 asylum seekers and had 4.49 million internally displaced and returned persons; government activities with UNHCR covered protection, education, health, food security, water, sanitation, shelter, energy, and site management. Refugee children were integrated into the national education system, but limited resources constrained capacity and primary education received priority.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.9","6B.3","6B.6","6B.10","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The population figures are from 2019 and do not describe 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the activities to the government with UNHCR support.","limitations":["No 2023 displacement or service-access figures are supplied.","The extraction does not quantify the share of displaced children actually reached."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1fbc524a4429d2b1","start_unit":136,"end_unit":140,"fact_summary":"The Mining Code prohibited child labor in mines and allowed penalties for rights violations; a 2014 survey estimated 40,000 children working in southeastern mines. The DRC adopted a national strategy in 2017 to eliminate child labor in artisanal mining by 2025, created a monitoring commission, and supported a five-year cobalt project funded at 84 million US dollars for databases, child withdrawal, education, vocational training, reintegration of 14,850 children, and socioeconomic conversion of 6,250 parents.","question_ids":["3B.7","5B.4","5B.5","6B.3","6B.7","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The evidence concerns 2014–2022 and a target extending to 2025; it does not establish 2023 results.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the legal framework and national strategy to the DRC government, with African Development Bank financing.","limitations":["The 40,000 estimate is from 2014.","The project’s reported targets are not equivalent to completed outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1fbc524a4429d2b1","start_unit":143,"end_unit":145,"fact_summary":"The government’s zero-street-children project operated in Kinshasa and Haut-Katanga with police child-protection units; in 2020, 22 children’s courts existed in 14 of 26 provinces with 72 assigned judges, but only 50 judges were effectively functioning, limiting court operations. In 2020, COVID-19 prison decongestion released 1,900 children, including 302 girls, and 123 of 145 released children in Kinshasa were reunited with families.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.7","3B.9","6B.2","6B.6","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The operational figures are from 2020 and do not establish the 2023 situation.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the projects and prison-decongestion decision to government ministries and authorities.","limitations":["The court staffing deficit indicates capacity constraints but not personal presidential responsibility.","The extraction does not report later judicial staffing or child outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1fbc524a4429d2b1","start_unit":147,"end_unit":149,"fact_summary":"The report states that Congolese legislation was weak and insufficiently explicit on judicial assistance for child victims and witnesses, although procedural provisions required counsel, allowed medical and psychological assessment, protected privacy through closed hearings, and recognized children’s right to be heard with counsel.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.7","6B.8","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The legal finding is not dated specifically to 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report describes Congolese legislation and does not attribute the gap or safeguards to a personal presidential act.","limitations":["The extraction does not show enforcement or access in practice.","The statement combines a general legislative deficiency with specific procedural protections."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1fbc524a4429d2b1","start_unit":150,"end_unit":153,"fact_summary":"The DRC’s action plan against recruitment and use of children in armed forces and groups had four pillars—separation, response, prevention, and combating impunity—and annual road maps; actions since 2017 removed the national army from the UN blacklist, but the country remained listed because children continued to be recruited by armed groups. In 2017, an estimated 5,000–10,000 children were associated with militias in Kasai, while more than 3,000 children were released from armed groups and nearly 1,000 in Kasai received support.","question_ids":["2B.4","2B.5","2B.9","3B.2","3B.7","3B.9","8B.1","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The facts concern 2017–2019 and do not establish the position in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the action plan and implementation to the DRC government with UN and partner support.","limitations":["The continued listing reflects armed-group recruitment, not necessarily government recruitment.","The extraction does not provide current 2023 figures or a causal evaluation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1fbc524a4429d2b1","start_unit":155,"end_unit":160,"fact_summary":"The government and partners trained military, police, judicial, and child-protection personnel on preventing child recruitment and sexual violence; 60 armed-group commanders were sensitized and 24 signed commitments not to recruit children or commit grave violations. Between July 2018 and June 2019, 2,366 children were separated from armed groups, including 805 voluntarily released and 1,561 who escaped or were handed over; 141 recruits identified as children were separated after verification.","question_ids":["2B.4","2B.5","2B.9","3B.2","3B.7","3B.9","8B.3","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The evidence is from 2018–2019 and does not measure 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the measures to the DRC government and international partners.","limitations":["Commitments and separations do not establish durable prevention or accountability.","The role of external actors is substantial."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1fbc524a4429d2b1","start_unit":162,"end_unit":165,"fact_summary":"Of 1,316 children reintegrated, 29 percent were girls; 523 received school reintegration, 441 vocational reintegration, and 382 economic reintegration. Separately, military justice actors were trained on investigations, and prosecutions produced convictions for several armed-group commanders, including life imprisonment for Dominique Byenge Birihanze and prison terms for other commanders accused of recruiting children.","question_ids":["2B.4","2B.9","3B.2","3B.7","6B.3","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The reintegration figures concern 2018–2019 and the convictions predate 2023; no 2023 update is provided.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes reintegration and military-justice actions to DRC authorities with MONUSCO and partner support.","limitations":["The extraction does not establish whether convictions were enforced or whether reintegration was durable.","The defendants’ conduct is reported as prosecuted, not independently adjudicated here."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["The supplied document is a DRC government periodic report received in 2023 but contains predominantly historical evidence from 2013–2022; it provides little evidence specifically occurring in 2023.","The extraction is severely corrupted by UTF-16/HTML artifacts, and several table units are fragmented; only facts recoverable from contiguous labeled units were used.","The report frequently describes government programs, plans, legal frameworks, and donor-supported activities without isolating Félix Tshisekedi’s personal decision, implementation control, or causal contribution.","No evidence in the supplied document materially addresses nuclear risk, nuclear posture, proliferation controls, or other existential-risk safeguards."]}
